headline: Cooper Investors initiated a position in Auckland International Airport as a high-quality monopoly infrastructure asset with strong long-term recovery prospects
reasoning: AIA is described as a highly attractive long-term infrastructure asset operating as a monopoly with a perpetual asset life. Tourism is one of New Zealand's key industries and AIA is the key gateway, having grown its share of international arrivals to around 75-80% pre-Covid. Over the 20 years prior to the pandemic, AIA delivered passenger growth at more than 2x GDP with 3-4% p.a. improvement in revenue per passenger. While Covid is the worst event AIA has faced, recovery following September 11 and the GFC was strong. Downside risks are partially mitigated by lower operating leverage, low current cash burn, a premium tangible asset base, conservative gearing and a dividend payout policy more conservative than Sydney Airport. Medium-term capex opportunities in property, car parking, retail and adjacent land development provide additional return potential.
quote: AIA is a highly attractive long term infrastructure asset operating as a monopoly with a perpetual asset life (unlike Sydney airport for instance). Tourism is one of New Zealand's key industries (of similar size to the Dairy industry), and AIA is the key gateway having grown its share of international arrivals significantly over the past decade to around 75-80% (pre-Covid). For the 20 years prior to the pandemic, AIA delivered growth in passengers at more than 2x GDP. AIA also saw a 3-4% p.a. improvement in revenue per passenger, underpinned by growth in international passengers (who are more valuable to AIA as they tend to spend more in Retail). Although Covid-19 is by far and away the worst event AIA has had to deal with, the last 20 years of operations and growth has included the events of September 11 and the global financial crisis. The recovery following these two prior events was strong.

headline: Greencape added Auckland International Airport to portfolios at attractive prices following March sell-off and April equity raise, citing Trans-Tasman bubble optionality and conservative balance sheet.
reasoning: Greencape had long admired AIA but struggled with its historically rich valuation relative to SYD; the COVID-19 sell-off and equity raise in April provided an attractive entry point. AIA handles approximately 75% of all international visitors to New Zealand and is the largest domestic airport by a factor of 3x the next largest, giving it a dominant market position. Domestic utilisation has recovered to 60-70% of pre-COVID levels, returning the company to approximately EBITDA breakeven. Greencape expects significant leverage to a near-term Trans-Tasman and potentially Pacific Island travel bubble, given approximately two-thirds of pre-COVID international passengers originated from NZ, Australia, and the Pacific Islands. AIA's NZD$2 billion investment property portfolio and 25% stake in Queenstown Airport provide additional value. A conservative post-raise balance sheet gives ample liquidity to navigate subdued operating conditions.
quote: Auckland International Airport is a relatively recent addition to the Greencape portfolios. We have long admired the company but struggled with the valuation at which the stock has historically traded, especially in comparison to SYD. With the stock selling off through March and the company raising equity in early April, we were able to add the stock to the portfolios at attractive prices. AIA is the gateway into New Zealand with approximately 75% of all international visitors arriving through its terminals. It is also the largest domestic airport in NZ by a factor of 3x the 2nd largest. In 'normal' times, 45% of the >20 million passengers passing through the airport are domestic passengers and with the recent lift in domestic utilisation back to 60-70% of pre-COVID levels, the company is back operating at approximately EBITDA breakeven.
